title: Podcast: Software Engineering Daily - Distributed Systems
content:
# Podcast: Software Engineering Daily - Distributed Systems

**Episode:** Distributed Consensus Algorithms
**URL:** https://softwareengineeringdaily.com/episode-442
**Date Listened:** 2025-01-12
**Duration:** 58 minutes
**Listen Time:** 10:00-11:00 AM

## Notes

[05:30] Introduction to CAP theorem - can't have all three: Consistency, Availability, Partition tolerance

[12:15] Raft algorithm explanation - simpler alternative to Paxos

[28:40] Real-world example: How Consul uses Raft for service discovery

[45:20] Discussion on eventual consistency vs strong consistency tradeoffs

## Key Takeaways

- Raft is more understandable than Paxos for most teams
- Choose consistency model based on use case, not ideology
- Testing distributed systems requires chaos engineering

## Follow-up

- Read Raft paper: https://raft.github.io/
- Check out Consul documentation
- Look into Jepsen for testing

title: Python Technical Documentation
content:
# Python Technical Documentation

## Virtual Environments

```bash
# Create venv
python -m venv .venv

# Activate (Unix)
source .venv/bin/activate

# Activate (Windows)
.venv\Scripts\activate
```

## Common Commands

```bash
# Install requirements
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Freeze dependencies
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Run tests
pytest tests/

# Type checking
mypy src/
```

## Useful Snippets

### Context Manager
```python
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def timer(name):
    start = time.time()
    yield
    print(f"{name}: {time.time() - start:.2f}s")
```

### Logging Setup
```python
import logging

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format='%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s'
)
```

title: Research: ML Model Optimization
content:
# Research: ML Model Optimization

## Goal

Improve inference speed for production ML models without sacrificing accuracy.

## Papers to Read

1. "Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network" (Hinton et al.)
2. "Quantization and Training of Neural Networks for Efficient Integer-Arithmetic-Only Inference"
3. "MobileNets: Efficient Convolutional Neural Networks for Mobile Vision Applications"

## Techniques to Explore

### Model Compression
- Pruning (remove unnecessary weights)
- Quantization (reduce precision)
- Knowledge distillation (smaller student model)

### Architecture Changes
- Depthwise separable convolutions
- Efficient attention mechanisms
- Mobile-optimized architectures

## Experiments
